tasks.title: Select the entire army with F3
tasks.why: Reinforcements should be easy to collect without dragging workers into combat.
acceptance: F3 and the Army button select owned combat units across the map.
Workers, buildings and opponents stay out of the selection.

tasks.title: Cancel queued units with a full refund
tasks.why: Misclicks and supply blocks need an immediate, predictable recovery action.
acceptance: Right-click an active or waiting unit in single or combined production queues to cancel it.
Refund exactly the paid crystal/aether and release its reserved supply.
Preserve all other queue entries and their progress.

tasks.title: Rally newly trained workers onto resources
tasks.why: The economy should obey a deliberate rally target instead of ignoring it.
acceptance: Right-click crystal or a friendly Aether Tap with a selected producer to set a resource rally.
New workers harvest that target; a ground rally moves them to the chosen position.
A destroyed/depleted resource target falls back safely; soldiers never harvest.

tasks.title: Prove smooth full-army battles
tasks.why: Responsiveness is the first quality bar; additional effects must fit the frame budget.
acceptance: Benchmark paid 100- and 200-supply armies at 1080p on documented hardware.
At normal speed target 60 FPS, p95 frame time under 16.7 ms and no stalls over 100 ms.
Report simulation, navigation, HUD, rendering and capture costs separately.
tasks.progress: Large-selection HUD layout caching is shipped. Full paid-army frame-budget targets remain unverified.

tasks.title: Add authoritative fog of war and scouting
tasks.why: Both player and enemy currently see too much; reconnaissance needs to matter.
acceptance: Track unexplored, explored and currently visible areas per player.
Use the same sight rules for targeting, rendering, minimap and built-in AI.
Last-seen structures persist; hidden moving enemies do not leak through bars or commands.

tasks.title: Keep large armies moving through real chokepoints
tasks.why: Local detours exist; whole-army arrival and narrow passages need stress-tested behavior.
acceptance: Test mixed 40/100/200-unit formations in both travel directions.
Units reach usable firing positions without jams, oscillation or pushing held units.
Preserve explicit move, attack-move and retreat intentions.

tasks.title: Save and resume missions exactly
tasks.why: A computer sleeping or a game restart should not discard an army-building session.
acceptance: Versioned manual saves and rotating autosaves restore resources, orders, queues, AI and RNG.
A resumed run matches an uninterrupted run at deterministic checkpoints.
Recover safely from interrupted writes and incompatible save versions.

tasks.title: Harden every command across focus and UI changes
tasks.why: Selection, held keys and modals already have regression tests; broader input coverage is needed.
acceptance: Cover windowed/fullscreen scaling, letterboxing, modifiers, focus loss and stuck buttons.
Repeated selection, production and placement inputs never issue unintended orders.
Keep a reproducible rendered input walkthrough for each regression.

tasks.title: Make the minimap a reliable tactical tool
tasks.why: Threats, rallies and objectives should be recognizable without moving the camera.
acceptance: Distinct friendly/enemy/structure/resource markers remain readable at every map size.
Add timed player pings, objective markers and useful attack alerts.
Minimap honors fog, camera bounds and left/right-click commands.

tasks.title: Read units and attacks at gameplay zoom
tasks.why: Original silhouettes and restrained effects should communicate who is firing at what.
acceptance: Differentiate infantry, armor, siege and support by silhouette and animation.
Tune muzzle flashes, impacts, trails, deaths and selection colors at common zoom levels.
Keep pooled effects within the measured frame budget.

tasks.title: Integrate and mix the concurrent audio work
tasks.why: Audio cues are being developed separately and need an integration pass.
acceptance: Coordinate with the audio changes before editing their files.
Selection, acknowledgement, attack and warning cues have distinct priorities and volume controls.
Limit overlapping voices and provide visual equivalents for critical warnings.
tasks.progress: Integrated the audio assets pushed to origin/main in a9719a8d. Pooled world/UI voices, event signals, separate cosmetic RNG, F8 volume and F11 mute. Verified actual WASAPI device activation separately from silent automation.

tasks.title: Offer readable health bars and team colors
tasks.why: Dense fights need clear damage and ownership without relying only on red/green.
acceptance: Options for always/selected/damaged health and shield bars persist.
Use shape/outline and colorblind-friendly palettes for ownership and warnings.
Keep text and bars legible on scaled and small displays.

tasks.title: Show worker allocation and resource saturation
tasks.why: Players need to see why income is weak and where extra workers should go.
acceptance: Show assigned versus useful crystal/aether workers at each base.
Select idle workers and depleted sites reliably.
Explain supply reservation and income in focused tooltips.

tasks.title: Add a global production and supply overview
tasks.why: Combined selection queues exist; macro should also be readable while the army is selected.
acceptance: Optional compact strip shows active production, idle producers and supply warning.
Clicking an entry selects or centers its producer without losing control groups.
Avoid covering the battlefield with decorative counters.

tasks.title: Allow custom hotkeys and camera speeds
tasks.why: A fixed layout should not be the only way to play comfortably.
acceptance: Remap unit, structure, control-group and camera actions with conflict validation.
Provide default and grid layouts; support keyboard layouts and reset-to-default.
Persist mouse speed and repeat timing without changing simulation speed.

tasks.title: Complete control-group and camera-location tools
tasks.why: Basic groups exist; splitting armies and returning to bases needs fewer steps.
acceptance: Add/remove/steal membership with clear modifier semantics.
Save/recall camera locations and cycle owned bases.
Death and selection changes do not leave stale or duplicate tags.

tasks.title: Explain target and command failures clearly
tasks.why: A rejected order should be understandable without opening logs.
acceptance: Show contextual feedback for range, terrain, minimum range, cooldown and invalid targets.
Display queued waypoints and destination feedback without visual spam.
Prioritize attack alerts and allow jumping to the relevant location.

tasks.title: Build coherent faction tech and upgrade choices
tasks.why: Unit abilities exist, but army progression needs explicit strategic tradeoffs.
acceptance: Define original upgrade paths, prerequisites, costs and research durations.
Expose the tech tree and unmet requirements in tooltips.
Prove paid research, stat effects and intended matchup shifts with thresholds.

tasks.title: Make the opponent scout and adapt honestly
tasks.why: Paid skirmish AI is a foundation; strategic choices should depend on available information.
acceptance: Scout, expand, defend and retreat using visible evidence.
Difficulty changes decisions rather than granting resources or hidden vision.
Run multiple paid build orders and seeds against each faction with outcome/time bounds.

tasks.title: Expose the full matchup matrix in Battle Lab
tasks.why: Automated roster/ability duels exist; players need accessible squad comparisons too.
acceptance: Choose both unit types, counts, upgrades, abilities and formations.
Run mirrored equal-supply/equal-cost fixtures with seeded replay.
Display win/loss thresholds, survivors, time-to-kill and trade efficiency.

tasks.title: Add mission variety and clear objective states
tasks.why: First Strike proves the build-and-assault loop; a campaign needs more than one static garrison.
acceptance: Add defense, escort and timed optional objectives with original maps and briefings.
Explain failure and recovery conditions; retain collapsible objectives and results.
Prove normal paid build paths for every mission without injected wins.

tasks.title: Teach the core loop through playable steps
tasks.why: New players should learn gathering, supply, production and attack-move in context.
acceptance: Highlight the relevant worker, button and target for each tutorial step.
Advance from observed outcomes instead of timers or forced state changes.
Allow skipping, replaying and practicing without an external AI service.

tasks.title: Record deterministic replays and desync checks
tasks.why: A bug or surprising result should be replayable from its actual inputs.
acceptance: Persist seed, version and ordered commands with checkpoint checksums.
Support playback speed, pause, timeline markers and an end report.
Detect incompatible versions and diverging state with useful diagnostics.

tasks.title: Develop a small, tested tactical map pool
tasks.why: Terrain and expansions should create meaningful choices instead of accidental path failures.
acceptance: Author original maps with distinct rush distances, chokes and expansion tradeoffs.
Validate worker routes, army passages, high-ground access and resource fairness.
Ensure editor round-trips preserve campaign metadata and playable geometry.

tasks.title: Extend results to macro decisions and match history
tasks.why: Battle combat statistics exist; economy and decision timing should also be inspectable.
acceptance: Track income, worker count, supply blocks, idle production and army value over time.
Keep resource accounting distinct from damage and production completion.
Save browsable match history with scenario/version/seed provenance.

tasks.title: Package and validate desktop builds
tasks.why: A polished game needs predictable startup, settings and recoverable failures.
acceptance: Build reproducible Windows/Linux packages with original assets and licenses.
Test startup, fullscreen/windowed changes, alt-tab, device changes and offline play.
Provide useful crash diagnostics and keep saved games across upgrades.

tasks.title: Design multiplayer only after deterministic foundations
tasks.why: Networking must preserve command responsiveness and fair information rules.
acceptance: Prototype command synchronization, checksums, lobby flow and disconnect recovery.
Apply authoritative fog and validate commands for the issuing player.
Measure latency and keep a reproducible two-client test before claiming multiplayer support.

tasks.title: Reuse stable large-army HUD selection layouts
tasks.why: Unchanged army selections were being sorted and laid out every rendered frame.
acceptance: Repeated layouts reuse cached geometry.
Selection, unit-type and production ownership changes invalidate the cache.
Health, movement and construction progress keep using live unit data.

tasks.title: Queue worker buildings then return to gathering
acceptance: Shift placement stays active and distributes group work.
Gathering yields after one delivery; one worker can complete multiple queued buildings.
Native live-clock input constructs three paid halls then returns all workers to crystal.

tasks.title: Cancel a foundation from its active worker
acceptance: N / Cancel Construction removes a foundation and refunds 75% of paid costs, rounded down.
Selecting the worker preserves construction; Halt remains distinct.
No double refund or combat-death accounting on cancellation.

tasks.title: Gas economy and a winding three-pass assault
acceptance: Mine campaign gas and pay for a Breacher, Workshop and Howitzer.
Clear two sentry posts before the final stronghold.
28 Riflemen lose; an assembled army of roughly 40 wins with meaningful losses.
